$comment: THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for how this pipeline carries values.
Every wall this codebase hit was one mistake said twice: an exact integer
carried in a float. Slot ordinals aliased past 2^24. Pick ID bases alias past
2^24. foldScalars lane 0 (totalRows) aliases past 2^24. Each layer decided,
independently and in a comment, what kind each field was, and the copies drifted.
KIND is the declared fact. CONTAINER is a per-layer realization of it.
count / identity / bitfield   exact. MUST NOT ride a float carrier — and a
float ordered key IS a float carrier wearing a
u32 costume, which is how totalRows hid.
measure                       a real quantity. f32 is correct and its
rounding is load-bearing.
Layers may realize kinds differently and stay conformant — the engine uses two
buffers (where a value lives IS its kind, so it cannot be got wrong), while the
TSL side uses one homogeneous atomic buffer where kind is per-lane. Neither is
privileged. What each layer owes is that its generator ASSERT its own mapping
respects the kinds, so both realizations are checkable rather than trusted.
The engine's two-buffer strides are DERIVED from kind below and asserted
against it, so its container cannot disagree with the declaration.

lanes.name: Y
lanes.note: Addressed POSITIONALLY as X+1 in glyphVertex.js — a search for S_Y misses that read.

lanes.name: Z
lanes.note: Addressed POSITIONALLY as X+2 in glyphVertex.js.

lanes.name: GLYPH_ID
lanes.misplaced: This is an IDENTITY living in the measures buffer. It is here only because it is copied verbatim from the trie's f32 blocks, so it cannot move until the TRIE FORMAT moves. It is the single exception in the system and it is deliberately visible: one identity, in the wrong array, naming its own fix.

lanes.name: FLAGS
lanes.note: Read with bitwise ops by later dispatches, so not render-scratch.

lanes.name: ORD
lanes.note: The lane that started all of this. Aliased past 2^24 as an f32; exact to 2^32 as a native count.

identities.name: slotOrdinal
identities.note: Per-ITEM, not per-arena: ord resets for each item.

identities.name: pickId
identities.witness: a readback for a known glyph must resolve to that glyph
identities.broken: Rides a FLOAT uniform today (uniform(0) from a JS number). Aliases past 2^24; the guard admits 0x7FFFFFFF, 127x too permissive, and WARNS rather than refuses. Reachable since the arena passed 2^24.

$comment: The segmented monoid's element (ScanElem), as it lives in a GPU buffer.
Same rule as the slot buffers: counts and measures are different arrays.
tail_adv is the ONLY measure — it is an f32 sum accumulated per-add, which
is what makes the reduce exact under regrouping. Everything else is a count.

lanes.name: RESET
lanes.note: absorbing: combine(a,b)=b when b.reset — file isolation is structural

lanes.name: WRAP
lanes.note: a QUERY parameter carried in the element, not file state

lanes.name: TAIL_ADV
lanes.note: f32 per add — the discipline that makes the reduce exact under regrouping

$comment: Per-item layout params as the GPU sees them. Authored f64 on the host and
NARROWED to f32 here, because Metal has no double precision — which is why
paginate on device is an eps-tier comparison rather than a bit-exact one.
HAS_PAGE is a flag riding this buffer; it is 0 or 1 and exact either way.
Per-item bounds + fold scalars. 8 lanes, and lane 6 is why this section exists.
TOTAL_ROWS is a COUNT (row + 1) that the TSL side stores via floatToOrderedKey —
an exact integer on a float carrier, aliasing past 2^24. Reachable: S_ROW is the
VISUAL row, so at wrap=1 rows track glyph count, crossing 2^24 at ~16.8MB inside
a 44.7MB arena. foldGeometry.js:146 has been doing Math.trunc(p.totalRows || 0) —
a consumer defensively truncating a count back to an integer, which is a
downstream compensating for an upstream that lost its type.
The engine's CPU form holds all 8 in f64, which is exact to 2^53 and has no wall,
so there is no defect there. On DEVICE it must split: Metal has no f64, and an
f32 ordered key would alias exactly as the TSL side does. The hardware forces the
same answer the kind rule already required.

lanes.name: TOTAL_ROWS
lanes.note: the fold scalar the TSL side carries as a float ordered key — see above

lanes.name: MAX_ROW_EXTENT
lanes.note: item-relative widest fold row; genuinely a measure, keeps the ordered key
